essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions split Europe into rival blocs and raised the risk that a local crisis could spread.

activities.label: Explain the start
activities.title: From Sarajevo to war
activities.body: In your own words, explain how the assassination turned into war. Keep it short and specific.
activities.concept: Sequence from the Sarajevo assassination to declarations of war
activities.correctAnswer: The Sarajevo assassination triggered the July Crisis, and the crisis escalated into declarations of war that widened the conflict.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names the assassination, the July Crisis, and the move to declarations of war in order.

activities.label: Fix the sequence
activities.title: What happens next
activities.body: Revise your answer using the correction. Write one cleaner version of the chain.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Thinking the assassination and the war were the same event, instead of the assassination leading into the July Crisis and then declarations of war.
activities.concept: Sequence from the Sarajevo assassination to declarations of war
activities.correctAnswer: The assassination was the trigger, not the whole war. It led into the July Crisis, and then declarations of war widened the conflict.
activities.feedback: Fix the order: trigger first, crisis second, declarations of war third.

activities.label: Rebuild the timeline
activities.title: World War I timeline
activities.body: Explain the full start-to-finish timeline in plain language. Include the start, U.S. entry, and the armistice.
activities.correctAnswer: World War I begins in 1914, the United States enters in 1917, and the war ends with the armistice in 1918.
activities.feedback: A complete answer places 1914, 1917, and 1918 in the correct order and names what each date marks.

activities.label: Check the big picture
activities.title: Best summary
activities.body: Choose the best summary of how the war began and unfolded.
choices: Europe was divided into rival alliance blocs, the Sarajevo assassination sparked the July Crisis, declarations of war widened the conflict, and the war ran from 1914 to the armistice in 1918.
The war began only because one assassination immediately caused all countries to enter at once.
World War I started in 1917 when the United States entered, and it ended before any major wartime escalation.
The armistice came before the United States entered, so the timeline runs backward from 1918 to 1917 to 1914.
activities.correctAnswer: Europe was divided into rival alliance blocs, the Sarajevo assassination sparked the July Crisis, declarations of war widened the conflict, and the war ran from 1914 to the armistice in 1918.
activities.feedback: The best summary connects causes, outbreak, and timeline in one chain.

items.essentialIdea: Prewar European alliances and tensions split Europe into opposing armed blocs before 1914.

check.title: European alliance blocs
check.prompt: How did prewar European alliances and tensions shape Europe before 1914?
check.referenceAnswer: They divided Europe into opposing armed blocs, raising the chance that a local crisis would spread. Rival alliances increased tension and made war more likely.
check.feedback: It is about bloc division and rising tension, not a single treaty.

items.essentialIdea: The Sarajevo assassination triggered July Crisis decisions that led Austria-Hungary to declare war on Serbia.

check.title: From Sarajevo to war
check.prompt: What sequence connects the Sarajevo assassination to the first declarations of war?
check.referenceAnswer: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand led Austria-Hungary into the July Crisis, then Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia. That decision set off the wider chain of war declarations.
check.feedback: The key link is the July Crisis between the assassination and the first declaration of war.

items.essentialIdea: World War I began in 1914 and ended in 1918 with the armistice.

check.title: War dates in order
check.prompt: What is the basic chronology of World War I from 1914 to 1918?
check.referenceAnswer: World War I began in 1914 and ended in 1918. The armistice ended the fighting in November 1918.
check.feedback: It needs both endpoints, not just one year.

recognitionCheck.title: World War I chronology
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which statement correctly describes World War I chronology?
choices: It began in 1914 and ended in 1918 with the armistice.
It began in 1918 and ended in 1914 with the armistice.
The Sarajevo assassination ended the war in 1914.
Prewar alliances removed tensions and prevented war.
recognitionCheck.correctAnswer: It began in 1914 and ended in 1918 with the armistice.
recognitionCheck.feedback: That is the correct basic chronology.

activities.label: Learn
activities.title: European alliance blocs
activities.body: Read the explanation, then answer the next question from memory.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions split Europe into opposing armed blocs before 1914.

activities.label: Explain
activities.title: European alliance blocs
activities.body: How did prewar European alliances and tensions shape Europe before 1914?
activities.concept: Prewar European alliances and tensions split Europe into opposing armed blocs before 1914.
activities.correctAnswer: They divided Europe into opposing armed blocs, raising the chance that a local crisis would spread. Rival alliances increased tension and made war more likely.
activities.feedback: It is about bloc division and rising tension, not a single treaty.

activities.title: From Sarajevo to war
activities.body: Read the explanation, then answer the next question from memory.

essentialIdeas: The Sarajevo assassination triggered July Crisis decisions that led Austria-Hungary to declare war on Serbia.
World War I began in 1914 and ended in 1918 with the armistice.

activities.label: Explain
activities.title: From Sarajevo to war
activities.body: What sequence connects the Sarajevo assassination to the first declarations of war?
activities.concept: The Sarajevo assassination triggered July Crisis decisions that led Austria-Hungary to declare
activities.correctAnswer: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand led Austria-Hungary into the July Crisis, then Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia. That decision set off the wider chain of war declarations.
activities.feedback: The key link is the July Crisis between the assassination and the first declaration of war.

activities.label: Explain
activities.title: War dates in order
activities.body: What is the basic chronology of World War I from 1914 to 1918?
activities.concept: World War I began in 1914 and ended in 1918 with the armistice.
activities.correctAnswer: World War I began in 1914 and ended in 1918. The armistice ended the fighting in November 1918.
activities.feedback: It needs both endpoints, not just one year.

activities.body: Which statement correctly describes World War I chronology?
